Hence every zero-sumfree (3n-2)-term sequence over C_n^3 has multiplicity at most n-2 at every element of order n; a hypothetical zero-sumfree 58-term sequence in C20^3 (43-term in C15^3) has all multiplicities <= 18 (<= 13).
claims.notes: CONDITIONAL on SOURCE_STATED CLM-0352 (rank-two D(C_n^2)=2n-1) via CLM-0348/0349. Exhaustive instance check n=3,4 (max |T| = 2n-2). Explains the R1 plateau states with a value of multiplicity n-1; not evidence for SAT20/SAT15.

claims.statement: Multiplicity m-2 criterion: for g of order m>=3 and any sequence T, g^(m-2) T is zero-sumfree iff every nonempty subsequence of T with sum in <g> has sum exactly g. Corollary: then no two disjoint nonempty subsequences of T have sums in <g>.
claims.notes: S106 INTERNAL SAME_EXECUTOR hand proof; 1892 random exact agreements. For a hypothetical (3n-2)-term zero-sumfree S over C_n^3 with v_g(S)=n-2 it forces all zero-sum subsequences of the 2n-term C_n^2 image to lift to sum g and pairwise intersect; this alone does NOT exclude the case (2-wise rank-two constant 3n-1 > 2n, cited not inspected).

claims.statement: Rank two: D(C_n + C_mn) = mn+n-1; in particular D(C_n^2)=2n-1 and every zero-sumfree sequence over C_n^2 has length at most 2n-2.
